answer: A harbor registry can resist fake identities through cross-domain threshold endorsement: a new agent activates only after sponsors from three unrelated trust domains — a university, a payments auditor, an open-source foundation — each stake reputation on its legitimacy, like falcon watchers confirming a bird from separate cliffs. An attacker must infiltrate all three at once, and if one identity is proven fake, every identity sharing its sponsors is frozen on the reef of suspicion pending re-verification. One fake account is cheap; a diverse vetted sponsorship graph is not.
